Harvard Classics, Vol. 26, Part 3

Phædra

Jean Racine

Recreating the spirit of classical antiquity, Racine draws upon 
Euripides
’s tragedy of 
Hippolytus
. Phædra falls in love with her stepson, Hippolytus, with tragic consequences. In Racine’s version, after being accused of rape and rejected by his father, Hippolytus is killed by a sea-monster. Phædra then commits suicide.
